hero.subtitle: When a defective product injures someone in Monterey, California law often lets them hold makers and sellers strictly liable without proving negligence. We can help you explore your legal options.

about.title: Monterey Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A defective product can turn an ordinary afternoon on Del Monte Avenue or Lighthouse Avenue into a trip to the emergency room. Monterey households buy everything from household appliances to bicycles, tools, and vehicle parts, and when one of those items fails because of a flaw in its design, manufacturing, or missing warning, California's strict liability rules generally allow an injured person to pursue the manufacturer, distributor, or retailer without having to prove anyone acted carelessly. That's a meaningful difference from typical negligence cases. If a defective product hurt you or someone in your family in Monterey County, keeping the item exactly as it was at the time of the injury matters — it may be the clearest evidence of what went wrong. We handle product liability matters and work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless money is recovered.
commonInjuries: Burns from malfunctioning appliances or batteries
Lacerations from broken glass or sharp component failure
Crush injuries from collapsing furniture or equipment
Traumatic brain injury from failed safety gear or helmets
Amputation or finger injuries from tool malfunctions
Poisoning or chemical exposure from mislabeled products

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Path
items.desc: Because California often applies strict liability to defective products, you may not need to show the manufacturer was careless — just that a defect existed and caused harm.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can each potentially be held liable, giving us more avenues to pursue on your behalf.

items.title: Evidence Preservation Matters Early
items.desc: Keeping the defective product intact can be critical to proving a design, manufacturing, or warning defect, and we can advise you on safeguarding it right away.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California's strict liability framework generally focuses on whether the product itself was defective and whether that defect caused your injury. This is often a lower bar than proving carelessness, though every case depends on its own facts.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to preserve it exactly as it was at the time of the injury, including packaging, instructions, or remaining parts. This evidence is often central to a Monterey product liability claim, and we can guide you on proper storage and documentation.

items.question: Is there a cost to speak with an attorney?
items.answer: No. We offer a free case review, and our team typically works on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover money.
